_doc: Item Workshop (hdart/puppet_items.py): equipment as overlay layers on the race's painted puppet, one layer per Template part it covers. zones: where an item may sit, as data (an editor comes later): part (fnmatch, e.g. arm*.upper), t = [from, to] along the part's bone (0 = start joint, 1 = end joint; <= 0 / >= 1 include the round ends), rows = [from, to] as fractions of the part's height (head, torso), ellipse = [cx, cy, rx, ry] as fractions of the part's box (curved edges), view = front / back (a zone for one view only), seam = above_waist / below_waist (+ seam_px to move the line down). bulk = px (1024 canvas) the item may paint beyond those zones. depth = stacking order (higher draws over lower). materials = colour keys the item is painted in; each becomes a channel (G of the levels map) coloured by a ramp of that material's palette group. clips = layers this item cuts away where it covers them (hair). kind held = generated alone on white and attached to a hand (grip), not painted on the body. Back view (like the back hair): a FLUX edit (`back_edit`) turns the painted front around; its item pixels guide the masked back pass, which takes that edit (not the front) as its reference.
prompt: {style}. One {body}, full body, three-quarter view facing left, seen slightly from above, standing in an A-pose, now wearing {item}. {materials} Clean dark outlines; the same face, head, skin and body, nothing else added. On a pure white background.
prompt_back: {style}. The same {body} seen from behind, three-quarter back view facing away to the right, seen slightly from above, standing in an A-pose, wearing {item}, its back side as in the reference image: the back of the garment over the shoulder blades and the spine; nothing from the front of the body (no chest shape). {materials} Clean dark outlines, on a pure white background.
prompt_held: {style}. A single {item} on its own, upright and vertical, pointing straight up, the handle at the bottom, seen from the side, centred, game item art. {materials} Clean dark outlines, on a pure white background.
material_text: The {name} parts are one flat vivid pure {word} colour (a colour key), shaded only with darker and lighter {word}.

_doc_game: Game items (R-002): a Workshop piece (an entry of items) belongs to the game item `item` (default: its own id); several pieces can make one game item (item.iron_breastplate = breastplate + pauldrons). slot is one of the game's art slots (requirements.json). game_items: what an intake file says about a NEW game item (one the game doesn't have yet): name, kind, slot (game slot), weaponType, text (one line for the game), materials (material -> default ramp id). Missing fields are derived from the pieces; items the game already has take all of this from the game's content.
